Rachel Cusk is the most talked about novelist of the year. Known for her critically acclaimed Outline trilogy and memoirs – A Life’s Work and Aftermath – Cusk’s work poses constant challenges: to form, the limits of character, identity and what it means to be a woman. Arguably, no writer working today has pushed the boundaries of contemporary writing and storytelling further. In her latest book, Life of M, Cusk tells the story of M, a film star and one of the most recognisable faces of our time. This portrait of fame, beauty and power has generated headlines and has prompted discussion and debate throughout the literary world. On December 7 Cusk joins us to speak publicly about the book on a UK stage for the first time. Live at Union Chapel, she will shed light on the craft of autofiction, and what Life of M reveals about life and reality. Don’t miss this exclusive opportunity to hear Cusk discuss Life of M and her work to date, and ask your questions in the audience Q&A.

https://unionchapel.org.uk/whats-on/cara.d: Over the past decade, Upon A Winter’s Night has become much more than a Christmas tour. For many audiences, it has become part of Christmas itself, a much-loved annual tradition and a return, year after year, to music that offers space for reflection, wonder and connection. Now, in its tenth anniversary year, Cara Dillon brings this celebrated show to Union Chapel once more: an evening of darkness and light, and the mystery at the heart of Christmas. Released in 2016, and entering at number one on the Indie Album Charts, Upon A Winter’s Night quickly established itself as a distinctive and atmospheric way into Christmas. Drawing on Celtic hymns, ancient carols, traditional folk songs and original material, it reaches beyond the familiar sounds of the season towards something older, deeper and far more enduring. There is a particular stillness at the heart of these songs: the darkness of winter, the promise of light, the joy of birth and renewal. Woven together with Dillon’s unmistakable voice and the moving musicality of her band, they create an evening that is both intimate and expansive. For Dillon, that spiritual dimension remains central. Her relationship with this repertoire is deeply felt, and her voice brings an extraordinary clarity to music in which the sacred and the earthly have always existed side by side. It’s this combination that has made Upon A Winter’s Night such an essential part of Christmas for so many.

https://unionchapel.org.uk/whats-on/eric.d: JANUARY BLUES FESTIVAL 2027 presents ERIC BIBB + special guests: TBC The January Blues Festival celebrates it's 10th anniversary year with the welcome return of bluesman Eric Bibb. With a career spanning five decades, over forty albums, three Grammy nominations, a multitude of Blues Foundation awards and countless more accolades, Eric Bibb has secured his legacy as a legendary figure in the blues and roots genre. Born into a lineage of activism, Eric's father, the late Leon Bibb, was a key figure in the civil rights movement, marching alongside Dr. Martin Luther King. Immersed in the Village folk scene during his youth, Eric Bibb found inspiration in the visits of luminaries like Bob Dylan, Joan Baez, and Pete Seeger. Influenced deeply by the sounds of Odetta, Richie Havens, and Taj Mahal, he synthesized these elements into a style uniquely his own. Beyond conventional genres, Eric Bibb is labeled a bluesman, but he defies categorization, seamlessly sliding between musical realms. Grounded in the folk and blues tradition with contemporary sensibilities, Bibb's music reflects his thoughts on current world events and his own lived experiences, whilst remaining entertaining, uplifting, inspirational and relevant. Bibb's catalogue is now over 40 albums strong. His 2024 album In The Real World, recorded at Peter Gabriel's Real World Studios received critical acclaim. Eric Bibb is more than a blues troubadour; he is a storyteller and philosopher. His legacy is not just in the notes he plays or the stages he graces but in the questions he poses and the hope he instills.

https://www.rigb.org/whats-on/how-build-.d: Engineer Roma Agrawal uses surprising materials to explore some whacky engineering challenges As an engineer on The Shard, an iconic London landmark, Roma Agrawal knows that steel and concrete are master materials for big pieces of a structure. But what happens when you throw all sense out the window, and use completely the wrong material to build stuff? For example, what about using gummy bears to make swimming pools? Meringue to make rocket insulation? Or even chocolate to make a bridge? Through these whacky combinations, Roma reveals the secrets of how materials work, and why engineers don’t normally attempt such stunts and stick the materials they know and love. https://www.rigb.org/whats-on/neuroscien.d: Parastoo Hashemi explores the chemistry of our brains, and asks whether we might be able to create a simple chemical test to diagnose mental health problems. As our physical health has steadily improved over the last century, our mental health continues to decline. Depression alone is one of the globe's most common ailments, affecting an estimated 300 million people. Diagnoses are based on behaviour and questionnaires, while medical treatments do not work for all those who take them, and dosage and type are determined on a trial-and-error basis. Furthermore, large-scale antidepressant drug discovery has been severely toned back by large pharmaceutical companies.

https://www.rigb.org/whats-on/new-normal.d: A series of three enlightening short talks uncovering the technology helping us overcome the severe impacts of changing weather systems, presented by the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology.
